stem: During a solar eclipse, Meera's teacher takes the class outside to observe the event. Which statement about watching the eclipse safely is correct?

options.text: It is unsafe to look directly at the Sun during a solar eclipse without proper protection, so Meera should use a pinhole projector or certified eclipse-viewing glasses.
It is safe to watch the eclipse by looking at the Sun's reflection in a steel plate or a hand mirror.
It is safe to look directly at the Sun during the eclipse as long as Meera wears ordinary dark sunglasses.
When only a thin crescent of the Sun remains visible, it is safe for Meera to look at it directly without any protection.

teacher.key_rationale: Direct viewing of the Sun during an eclipse damages the eyes even when most of the Sun is covered; safe observation requires certified eclipse glasses or indirect projection. Options B, C and D each present a common but unsafe viewing idea, so only A is correct.
